links.note: Four sub-questions; the first and the one the answer opens on is the features of intensive subsistence farming (labour intensive, high biochemical inputs and irrigation) - 23963. The rest reach 23966 (rabi crops), 23970 (leguminous crops) and 23974 (minimum support price) one line each.

Six crossword clues; two of them are the two distinct halves of 23970's description - pulses as the source of protein, and jowar as a coarse grain. 23971 also takes two clues (tea/coffee, cotton), but 23970 matches more of the item's own words. NOTE: clue 2 keys 'Kharif' for 'the summer cropping season', which the chapter calls the monsoon season - zaid is its summer season.

The stem's organising idea is the kharif season and which food crop is its main one, so 23967. 23969 holds rice as a staple cereal in its own right; here rice is the answer to a question about the season.
The rabi counterpart of qid:105948 - wheat as rabi's main food crop, so 23966.
Rajasthan as the largest bajra producer; bajra is one of the three coarse grains 23970 names.

Maize needing 21-27 degrees C and old alluvial soil. Maize is a coarse cereal, placed in the text between the millets and the pulses, so 23970 is its home; 23969 covers only the staple pair rice and wheat.
Sugarcane's 21-27 degrees C and 75-100 cm rainfall - sugarcane is the first cash crop 23971 names.
Sericulture as the rearing of silkworms for silk fibre comes from the fibre-crops passage (cotton, jute, hemp, natural silk), which sits inside 23971's cash-crop group.
Jute as the golden fibre - one of 23971's named cash crops, against cotton, hemp and silk from the same fibre list.

The stem says 'primitive subsistence agriculture' but the keyed feature is 23962's description verbatim - when soil fertility decreases the farmer shifts and clears a fresh patch. Slash and burn is the specific mechanism inside primitive subsistence farming, and it is what the key tests; distractor A (large amount of labour) is 23963, which is how the item separates the two.

The right of inheritance dividing land among successive generations is the pressure-on-land clause of 23963, intensive subsistence farming in areas of high population pressure. The distractors paraphrase the same passage's consequences.
Punjab as the rabi state - it heads the list of states important for wheat and other rabi crops, so 23966.
Precipitation from western temperate cyclones in winter aiding rabi crops is the sentence inside 23966's rabi passage.
